subject: Group size code from 'old' inlabru tutorials

messages.author: 6016d2d465399879
messages.subject: Group size code from 'old' inlabru tutorials
parts:
Hi,

I am struggling to get result from for group size with code from the 'old' inlabru workshop on inlabru.org website.
on slide 8 and beyond in document 10_1d_groups.pdf in the 'old' workshop / tutorial from the .
This code was written for an older version of inlabru, and I can't quite figure out how to adjust it for the latest version. Any pointer would be greatly appreciated!

Many thanks in advance!

The code in question is on slide 8 and following in document 10_1d_groups.pdf  (and associated practical). I reproduce the first part below.

cmp = ~ log.r + Intercept
fml = size ~ dexp(size, rate = exp(log.r), log = TRUE) + Intercept
E_scale <- 1e5
fit = lgcp(cmp, groups, formula = fml, domain = list(size = c(0,40)), E = E_scale )

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Group size code from 'old' inlabru tutorials
parts:
Newer syntax would be something like this:

cmp = ~ log.r(1)+ Intercept(1)

fml = size ~ dexp(size, rate = exp(log.r), log = TRUE) + Intercept 
E_scale <- 1e5

fit = lgcp(cmp, data = groups, formula = fml,
domain = list(size = INLA::inla.mesh.1d(0:40,boundary=“free”)): E = E_scale )

The changes are mainly pricing a bit more specifics from the user.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Group size code from 'old' inlabru tutorials
parts:
It's a logic bug in the predictor evaluation code. The include
argument will be used if you supply _some_ data object.
newdata=data.frame() is sufficient.

I'll fix the bug, but also add code to eliminate the need for
"include" in most cases.

Finn
